data.analysis: I choose N=4 because the kernel has four distinct, testable opportunities: reuse source particles across output threads, reduce per-pair arithmetic, expose source-axis parallelism, and tune launch/work granularity. The supplied kernel performs an O(N²) pair loop with a square root and division per pair; source reuse is a plausible cost, but no profile establishes the bottleneck. The baseline is reported valid and correct, with three aggregate timing repetitions and mean 0.0018526378 s; per-size timings and independent confirmation are not supplied. Therefore, these are research hypotheses, and all comparisons must use the official correctness checks and geometric-mean kernel-time objective. The trees must preserve the fixed entry, Particle layout, full-state output, masses, and single-kernel interface for every valid input.

children.objective: Explore block-cooperative shared-memory tiling of source particles while retaining one output target per thread. Stage source records cooperatively, reuse each tile across the block’s target calculations, handle partial tiles and output tails safely, and obey the shared-memory limit. Preserve complete output coverage under the configured grid geometry. Measure against the baseline and validate all required sizes, coincident positions, extreme-mass case, and varying dt inputs; report correctness and repeated timing evidence.
children.subject: Shared-memory reuse of source particles

children.objective: Isolate pairwise arithmetic improvements in the one-thread-per-target loop. Evaluate direct rsqrtf-based reciprocal-distance arithmetic and mathematically valid removal of the target-mass factor, with any reassociation or FMA changes treated as hypotheses requiring validation. Do not enable global fast math or assume inputs are benchmark-specific. Check numerical tolerance, finite outputs, and exact mass preservation across all required cases before timing.
children.subject: Pairwise arithmetic and reciprocal-square-root optimization

children.objective: Explore a single-kernel mapping that assigns lanes within a warp to different source particles for one or more target rows, then reduces force components. Handle arbitrary N and tails without assuming a multiple of warp width; preserve the required float32 behavior within tolerance and avoid additional launches or buffers. Measure the full official size set because coalescing and reduction costs may outweigh added parallelism.
children.subject: Warp-parallel source-axis computation and reductions

children.objective: With the baseline-style source loop and without shared-memory tiling or warp reductions, investigate launch geometry and output work granularity. Tune block and items_per_block within the stated ranges, using a correct grid-stride mapping so every particle is written for all supported configurations and sizes. Compare repeated official timings and correctness; report the selected configuration and evidence rather than assuming larger blocks or more work per block are faster.
children.subject: Launch geometry and grid-stride work granularity
